comparison: Perfect agreement on claims (C6, C56-C59) regarding molecular dynamics simulations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the computational evidence is strong but suggests experimental validation would strengthen it. Peer reviewers accepted the structural mechanism without raising specific concerns about the simulation data itself.

Perfect agreement on claims (C51-C55, C78-C83) regarding EMT markers, migration/invasion assays, and functional consequences. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes context-dependency limitations, while peer reviewers accepted the findings after revision, noting stronger cause-effect relationships in the revised manuscript.

Strong disagreement on claims (C60-C70) regarding SHANK2 interactions with endosomal proteins. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with convergent biochemical and imaging data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to serious concerns about mass spec data quality, lack of SHANK2 enrichment in IP, missing mock controls, and inadequate co-localization methods.

Strong agreement on claims (C71-C77) regarding FAK/cortactin phosphorylation and pathway dependencies. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency across cell lines and multiple approaches. Peer reviewers accepted these findings after revision, noting the use of multiple approaches was convincing.

Agreement on claims (C84-C87) regarding in vivo xenograft and metastasis data. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest sample sizes (n=5). Peer reviewers accepted findings but requested ANOVA analysis and noted the assay is more of a lung colony assay that misses invasion aspects.

Strong disagreement on claims (C5, C34-C43) regarding PRMT7-mediated methylation of SHANK2. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to critical concerns about PRMT5 contamination in FLAG-IPs, SDMA antibody specificity issues, and whether PRMT7 specifically catalyzes this modification.

Disagreement on claims (C4, C30-C33) regarding PRMT7-SHANK2 interaction identification. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on mass spec, CoIP, and GST pull-down data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about low peptide counts (only 11 PRMT7 peptides), poor enrichment, potential PRMT5 contamination, and lack of mock controls.

Agreement on claims (C44-C50) regarding clinical correlations with breast cancer subtypes and TCGA analysis. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes correlative nature limits causal inference and modest sample sizes. Peer reviewers cite underpowered analyses, concerns that PRMT7 may be increased in all breast cancers (not just metastatic), and need for larger datasets and ANOVA analysis.

Partial overlap on claims (C10-C13, C88) regarding clinical correlations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for patient sample analyses showing correlations with aggressiveness, noting correlative limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, using cautious language ('appear' to correlate) and requesting additional patient characteristics and analysis of how stage/staining correlates with subtype.

Strong agreement on claims (C92-C98) regarding speculative roles in endocytosis and organelle localization. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are largely speculative/inferential requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers did not validate these speculations and raised concerns about mass spec data quality and requested removal of proteins not included in results tables.

Partial overlap on claims (C89-C91, C99-C100) regarding therapeutic potential and broader implications. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting therapeutic potential is reasonable inference but untested. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for overarching conclusions after revision, accepting that SHANK2 methylation may be a target for preventing metastasis.

Minimal overlap on claim C3 (background/framing claims). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as established literature appropriately cited. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for overarching conclusions, accepting the main findings after revision that drew stronger cause-effect relationships.

Peer review R11 addresses overarching conclusions (C3, C8-C9, C89-C91, C99-C100) that span multiple OpenEval results. Peer reviewers accepted the main conclusions after revision, finding the PRMT7-SHANK2-FAK mechanism and therapeutic implications SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluated these claims distributed across multiple results (R7, R8, R9) with mixed evaluations.
